why: "Some kind of queen?" came back as "Какой-то королевой?", the next sentence's verb pulled through the question mark. "Какой-то королева?" fails it too: the case is right and the gender is not

why: the other side of "Some kind of queen?": a fragment does take its case from the question it answers, and "Кого?" asks for the accusative. A rule that only said fragments stand alone would turn "Сестру?" into "Сестра?". Not asked with "Who did you call?": the model writes "Кого ты звонил" there 9 runs out of 10, which would test the verb rather than the fragment

why: the rule says to add whatever preposition the target needs, with "ждал час" becoming "waited for an hour". Russian needs none, and the error in this direction is the stilted one
text: I waited an hour and then left

why: the copula rule exists to put "to be" back for English. Into Russian the same rule read literally would add "есть", which no one says
text: he is a doctor and she is a teacher

why: the rule teaches that "Молодец" is "Well done", never a noun. The same phrase coming back the other way is the part no case covers

why: agreement is the rule that matters most when the target is Russian and least when it is English, and every case in this corpus so far had English as the target
text: the new coffee is really good

why: the idiom rule is one of the two written the right way round, with a Russian answer. Worth a case that is not the rule's own example

why: the borrowing rule shows Spanish "todo bien" becoming "everything is fine", not "everything is ok". Into Russian the same slide is to "всё окей"

why: "Who did you call yesterday? Your mom?" came back as "Кого ты звонил вчера?" 9 runs out of 10: звонить takes the dative, "Кому ты звонил?". With the cases beside it this asks whether that is one verb, or every verb that takes a direct object in English and the dative in Russian
text: Who did you call yesterday?

why: the same verb with no question word in front of it, to tell the verb's fault from the question's. "Набери меня" would be right too and fails this, so read a failure before counting it
text: Call me tomorrow.

why: another verb of the same kind: помочь takes the dative, "помочь брату", never "помочь брата"
text: Can you help my brother with the move?

why: верить takes the dative too: "Ты ему веришь?", never "Ты его веришь?"
text: Do you believe him?

why: передать привет takes the dative: "Передай маме привет", never "маму"
text: Tell your mom I said hi.

why: the other side of the dative cases: видеть takes the accusative, "сестру", so a rule about the dative read too widely would show up here as "сестре"
text: Did you see my sister yesterday?
